limitations: Native Windows, Linux and WSL2 not executed. Minimum Git version for cwd-relative HEAD:./ resolution inside cat-file --batch not verified on an older Git; on a Git that does not honour it the reply would be 'missing', which counts as differing, so the failure direction is safe. No 'ambiguous' reply could be produced for a HEAD:./ path. Implementation notes for the implementer: (1) the existing test_head_read_failure_or_timeout_counts_as_differing triggers on 'show' in cmd and would pass vacuously after the change because its document really differs; retarget it to cat-file and use a date-only document so only the fallback can stamp; (2) parse by input order, accept the two-token '<oid> submodule' reply and any non-blob type as differing while consuming <size> bytes plus LF for sized replies; (3) run in bytes mode, never text=True (utf-8 replace would break sizes); (4) keep per-document ValueError and encoding failures (relative_to, os.fsencode) per document so one odd path cannot fail the whole batch; (5) count only cat-file calls in AC-1 since collect_changed_markdown_paths also goes through _run_tree_kill; (6) choose and state a timeout that fits the 180 s caller limit alongside the 120 s git diff, and say in the tool reference that a failed batch stamps every candidate whose version was not obtained.

Executed in a scratch repo on Git 2.54.0 macOS: cat-file --batch with HEAD:./<path> returns '<oid> blob <size>\n<bytes>\n' per name in input order; names with spaces, double quote, non-ASCII, leading dash, colon, trailing space and an embedded CR all resolved; a zero-length blob gives 'blob 0' plus the trailing LF; a blob whose body looks like a header is parsed correctly by size; a symlink gives its target as a blob (same as git show); a path naming a tree returns 'tree <size>' with a binary body; a submodule path returns '<oid> submodule' with no size and no body (not a 'missing' line); an absent path returns '<input name> missing'. git -C <subdir> resolves HEAD:./ relative to the subdir, and with root equal to the top level. 5,000 names (19.8 MB output) completed through both run_with_tree_kill and isolated_run with no pipe deadlock, about 3.4 s warm; 500 names 0.4 s; 200 per-document git show calls 7.8 s. textconv and smudge config do not alter either git show or cat-file output, so the bytes compared are identical. The coarser failure in requirement 3 is stated in the Decision Log and Risks and is consistent with the shipped tool-reference wording, which limits the date-only promise to a readable HEAD version. AC-1 is observable with a delegating wrapper on dg._run_tree_kill that counts cat-file argv and calls the real resolver.
